verdict.rationale: Vercel docs support connecting existing Git providers (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) with push-to-deploy, zero-config Next.js and 40+ other frameworks, plus a standard CLI usable from any editor/terminal — suggesting minimal proprietary lock-in for source control and framework choice. However, community evidence directly contradicts the 'no proprietary tooling' framing: one commenter states 'There is no serious reason to use Vercel, other than for those being locked into the NextJs ecosystem,' and another complains 'I dislike how Vercel and Netlify build up on AWS and then we only get JS/TS/Go, or WebAssembly gimmicks,' indicating real limits on language/framework freedom and CI substitution (Vercel's own build pipeline replaces external CI). Missing for 10: evidence of explicit third-party CI integration (e.g., GitHub Actions coexistence), editor-specific tooling requirements, and rebuttal to the lock-in claims.
